title: The Brain's Needs, the Neuro Exam, and Decreased LOC
next: Chapter 31, Lesson 2: Stroke, TIA, seizures and syncope

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already check AVPU, protect the airway, give oxygen, check glucose, and give oral glucose, glucagon or naloxone. Today, as a PCP:

  1. Know what the brain needs, and why skull pressure matters
  2. Run a deeper neuro exam: GCS, posturing, Cushing reflex, speech
  3. Know what the PCP adds for decreased LOC: IV, D10W, IV naloxone

Textbook: Chapter 31, PDF pages 2804–2855
slides.say: Welcome to class. This is the first of two lessons on neurologic emergencies. As EMRs, you already check AVPU, protect the airway, give oxygen, check the blood sugar, and give oral glucose, glucagon and naloxone. Now that you're practising as a PCP, more is expected. You need to understand why the brain fails, so your exam finds the problem early. And you have new tools: an IV, a new sugar drug called D10W, and a new route for naloxone. Today we'll cover three things: what the brain needs, a deeper neuro exam, and exactly what the PCP adds for a patient with a decreased level of consciousness.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎来上课。这是神经系统急症两节课里的第一节。作为 EMR，你们已经会用 AVPU 评估意识、保护气道、给氧、测血糖，也会给口服葡萄糖、胰高血糖素和纳洛酮。现在以 PCP 身份执业，要求更高：你要理解大脑为什么会出问题，查体才能更早发现异常。你还有了新工具：静脉通路、一种叫 D10W 的新的补糖药，以及纳洛酮的新给药途径。今天讲三件事：大脑需要什么；更深入的神经系统检查；以及意识水平下降的病人，PCP 具体多做什么。

slides.title: What the brain needs
slides.body:
Oxygen, glucose, normal temperature

  • The brain burns glucose fastest and can't store it
  • Midbrain (RAS): wakefulness and level of consciousness
  • Pons: rhythm and depth of breathing
  • Medulla: heart rate, blood pressure, breathing rate

Any change in LOC: check all three needs.
slides.say: Let's start with the basics. The brain needs three things: oxygen, glucose, and a normal temperature. Glucose is its fuel. The brain burns it faster than any other part of the body, but it can't store any, so when sugar or oxygen runs low, the brain shows it first. It also helps to know where vital functions live in the brainstem. The midbrain holds the reticular activating system, which keeps us awake. The pons sets the rhythm and depth of breathing. The medulla controls heart rate, blood pressure and breathing rate. So when you see consciousness, breathing pattern, or pulse change, picture which part of the brain is under stress.
slides.sayZh: 先从基础说起。大脑需要三样东西：氧、葡萄糖和正常体温。葡萄糖是大脑的燃料，大脑消耗它比身体任何部位都快，却一点也存不住，所以糖或氧一不够，大脑最先表现出来。还要知道生命功能在脑干的哪个位置：中脑有网状激活系统，让人保持清醒；脑桥决定呼吸的节律和深度；延髓控制心率、血压和呼吸频率。所以当你看到意识、呼吸型态或脉搏发生变化时，要想到是大脑的哪个部位在受压。

slides.title: Pressure in the skull: ICP and CPP
slides.body:
CPP = MAP − ICP

  • The skull is a closed box: brain, blood, CSF
  • Normal MAP 70–100; normal ICP 5–15 mm Hg
  • Normal CPP 60–80 mm Hg; below 50, the brain becomes ischemic
  • High ICP or low BP: both starve the brain

Book: anyone at risk of high ICP needs a systolic of at least 110–120 mm Hg.
slides.say: Now one formula. The skull is a closed box holding brain, blood, and CSF, or cerebrospinal fluid. If bleeding, swelling or a tumour adds volume, the pressure inside, the ICP or intracranial pressure, rises. The pressure that pushes blood into the brain is the CPP, cerebral perfusion pressure. It equals the mean arterial pressure, or MAP, minus the ICP. Normal MAP is seventy to one hundred and normal ICP is five to fifteen, so normal CPP is sixty to eighty. Below fifty, the brain becomes ischemic. Here's the trap: CPP falls when ICP rises, but also when the blood pressure drops. That's why the book wants a systolic of at least one hundred ten to one hundred twenty in these patients.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲一个公式。颅骨是一个封闭的盒子，里面装着脑组织、血液和 CSF，也就是脑脊液。出血、水肿或肿瘤一旦增加体积，颅内的压力，也就是 ICP 颅内压，就会升高。把血推进大脑的压力叫 CPP，脑灌注压，等于平均动脉压 MAP 减去 ICP。正常 MAP 是七十到一百，正常 ICP 是五到十五，所以正常 CPP 是六十到八十；低于五十，大脑就开始缺血。陷阱在这里：ICP 升高会让 CPP 下降，血压下降也一样。所以书里要求这类病人收缩压至少一百一十到一百二十。

slides.title: Rising ICP: the Cushing reflex
slides.body:
SignRising ICPShock
Blood pressurerisesfalls
Pulse pressurewidensnarrows
Pulseslowsspeeds up
Breathingslows, abnormal patternspeeds up

Also: decorticate or decerebrate posturing; pupils unequal by > 1 mm.
slides.say: As ICP rises, the body fights back with the Cushing reflex. The medulla pushes the heart harder, so the systolic pressure climbs. As the brainstem gets squeezed, the vessels relax, the diastolic falls, and the pulse pressure widens. Finally, heart rate and breathing slow down. That is the exact opposite of shock, where pressure falls, the pulse pressure narrows, and the heart races. So in an unresponsive patient, a slow pulse with a high blood pressure is a brain warning, not reassurance. Other red flags are abnormal posturing, abnormal breathing patterns, and pupils that differ by more than one millimetre. Any of them means a critical patient.
slides.sayZh: ICP 升高时，身体会用库欣反射来对抗。延髓让心脏更用力收缩，所以收缩压上升；脑干受压后血管放松，舒张压下降，脉压增宽；最后心率和呼吸都变慢。这和休克正好相反：休克是血压下降、脉压变窄、心跳加快。所以在一个无反应的病人身上，脉搏慢加血压高是大脑在报警，不是让你放心的信号。其他危险信号还有异常姿势、异常呼吸型态，以及两侧瞳孔相差超过一毫米。出现任何一项，都按危重病人处理。

slides.title: GCS: one common language
slides.body:
Eyes1–4opens on own = 4
Verbal1–5oriented = 5
Motor1–6obeys = 6
  • Motor 3 = abnormal flexion (decorticate)
  • Motor 2 = abnormal extension (decerebrate): deeper damage
  • BC TBI bands: ≥ 13 mild, 9–12 moderate, ≤ 8 severe
slides.say: The Glasgow Coma Scale, or GCS, gives everyone the same language. Eyes score one to four, verbal one to five, and motor one to six, so the total runs from three to fifteen. Look closely at the motor score. If the patient bends the arms toward the chest on a painful stimulus, that's decorticate posturing, and it scores three. If the arms go stiff and straight and turn palms-down, that's decerebrate posturing. It scores two, and it's worse, because the damage is lower, near the brainstem. BC's head injury protocol uses three bands: thirteen or more is mild, nine to twelve is moderate, eight or less is severe. Repeat the GCS; the trend tells the story.
slides.sayZh: 格拉斯哥昏迷评分，也就是 GCS，让大家用同一种语言。睁眼一到四分，语言一到五分，运动一到六分，总分从三到十五。要仔细看运动分：疼痛刺激时病人把双臂屈向胸前，是去皮质姿势，得三分；双臂僵直伸展、掌心朝下转，是去大脑姿势，得两分，而且更严重，因为损伤位置更低、靠近脑干。BC 颅脑外伤流程分三档：十三分以上为轻度，九到十二为中度，八分以下为重度。GCS 要反复评，趋势最能说明问题。

slides.q: A 58-year-old had a sudden severe headache, then became unresponsive. BP 196/88, pulse 48, breathing slow and irregular. What do these signs most suggest?
options: Normal vital signs for her age
slides.say: Let's pause for a question. A fifty-eight-year-old had a sudden severe headache, then became unresponsive. Her blood pressure is one ninety-six over eighty-eight, her pulse is forty-eight, and her breathing is slow and irregular. What do these signs most suggest? A, compensated shock from hidden bleeding. B, rising intracranial pressure, the Cushing reflex. C, simple fainting. D, normal vital signs for her age. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 停一下考考你：一位五十八岁的女士突然剧烈头痛，随后失去反应。血压一百九十六比八十八，脉搏四十八，呼吸慢而不规则。这些体征最提示什么？A 隐匿出血导致的代偿期休克；B 颅内压升高，也就是库欣反射；C 单纯晕厥；D 这个年龄的正常生命体征。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B, rising intracranial pressure. A high systolic pressure, a wide pulse pressure, a slow pulse and slow, irregular breathing make up the Cushing reflex, and the sudden severe headache suggests a bleed. A is wrong because shock gives the opposite picture: low pressure and a fast pulse. C is wrong because fainting is brief and the patient wakes quickly. D is wrong: these signs are dangerous at any age.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B，颅内压升高。收缩压高、脉压宽、脉搏慢、呼吸慢而不规则，正是库欣反射，而突发剧烈头痛提示颅内出血。A 错，休克的表现正好相反：血压低、心跳快。C 错，晕厥时间很短，病人很快就醒。D 错，这些体征在任何年龄都很危险。

slides.title: Speech and understanding
slides.body:
FindingWhat you seeQuick test
Receptive aphasiaspeaks clearly, can't understandask the month; no yes/no
Expressive aphasiaunderstands, can't get words out"Raise your arm", then "Your name?"
Agnosiacan't name a common objectshow a pen: "What is this?"
Apraxiacan't use the object"Show me how you use it"

Global aphasia = both. The patient may still think clearly.
slides.say: Speech problems tell you a lot, and as a PCP you should describe them precisely. In receptive aphasia, the patient speaks clearly but can't understand you. Ask questions you both know the answer to, like what month it is, not yes-or-no questions. In expressive aphasia, the patient understands but can't get the words out: ask them to raise an arm, then ask their name. Agnosia means they can't name a common object, like your pen. Apraxia means they can't show you how to use it. A patient with global aphasia has both problems, but may still think clearly. So speak calmly, keep eye contact, explain and ask before you touch, and assume they understand you.
slides.sayZh: 言语问题能告诉你很多，作为 PCP 要描述得准确。感受性失语：病人说话清楚，但听不懂你，要问你们俩都知道答案的问题，比如现在是几月，不要问是非题。表达性失语：病人听得懂，但说不出来，先让他抬手，再问他叫什么名字。失认是叫不出常见物品的名字，比如你的笔；失用是不会演示怎么用。完全性失语两种问题都有，但病人可能仍然思路清楚。所以要平静地说话，保持眼神交流，触碰前先解释并征得同意，并假定他听得懂你。

slides.title: Movement, sensation and glucose
slides.body:
• Hemiparesis: one-sided weakness; hemiplegia: one-sided paralysis
  • Most motor nerves cross: the left brain moves the right body
  • Pronator drift: eyes closed, arms out; one arm drifts down
  • Unsteady walk, clumsy movement (ataxia): cerebellum
  • Glucose: normal 4–7 mmol/L; below 4, LOC starts to fall
  • Below 2: usually confused or unconscious
slides.say: Next, movement and sugar. Look for weakness on one side, called hemiparesis, or paralysis on one side, called hemiplegia. Most motor nerves cross over, so a problem in the left side of the brain weakens the right side of the body. A quick test is pronator drift: eyes closed, both arms held straight out; if one arm drifts down, think stroke. An unsteady walk or clumsy movement, called ataxia, points to the cerebellum. And never skip the glucose. Normal is four to seven millimoles per litre. Below four, the level of consciousness starts to fall, and below two, most patients are confused or unconscious. Every altered patient gets a sugar check.
slides.sayZh: 接着看运动和血糖。注意一侧无力，叫偏侧无力；一侧瘫痪，叫偏瘫。大多数运动神经会交叉，所以左侧大脑出问题，会让右侧身体无力。一个快速检查是旋前肌漂移试验：病人闭眼、双臂向前平举，如果一只手臂往下漂，要想到卒中。步态不稳或动作笨拙，叫共济失调，提示小脑问题。血糖绝对不能漏：正常是每升四到七毫摩尔；低于四，意识开始下降；低于二，多数病人会意识混乱或昏迷。每个意识改变的病人都要测血糖。

slides.title: General care for decreased LOC
slides.body:
1. Scene safety; airway and breathing; O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  2. Check glucose; treat a confirmed low
  3. Look for opioids and other drugs
  4. Temperature: warm the cold, cool the hot
  5. High ICP signs: head up 30° unless spine concern
  6. If ventilating: 16–20/min, no routine hyperventilation
slides.say: Here's the general approach for any patient with a changed level of consciousness, before you know the cause. Make the scene safe, then secure the airway and breathing; in BC, titrate oxygen to a saturation of ninety-four percent or more. Check the sugar and treat a confirmed low. Look for drugs, especially opioids. Check the temperature, and warm or cool the patient. If you see signs of high ICP, raise the head thirty degrees, unless you're worried about the spine. If you're ventilating, give sixteen to twenty breaths a minute. Don't hyperventilate routinely: blowing off too much carbon dioxide narrows the brain's vessels and cuts its blood flow.
slides.sayZh: 下面是任何意识改变病人的通用处理，在你还不知道病因之前就开始。先确保现场安全，再保证气道和呼吸；在 BC，按需给氧，使血氧饱和度维持在百分之九十四以上。测血糖，确认偏低就纠正。查找药物，尤其是阿片类。测体温，冷的保暖，热的降温。如果有颅内压升高的征象，床头抬高三十度，除非你担心脊柱损伤。如果需要辅助通气，每分钟十六到二十次。不要常规过度通气：二氧化碳排得太多会让脑血管收缩，脑血流反而减少。

slides.title: EMR vs PCP: decreased LOC in BC
slides.body:
BC Diabetic Emergencies protocol: known diabetics with decreased LOC, and decreased LOC with no known cause.

All licence levels (EMR + PCP)

  • Airway: position, suction, adjuncts
  • O₂ to SpO₂ ≥ 94%; lateral or ¾ prone if needed
  • Vital signs incl. glucose; look for stroke signs
  • BGL < 4.0 and airway safe: glucose gel
  • EMR: glucagon if the airway isn't protected

PCP adds

  • Vascular access (IV)
  • Confirmed low: D10W 10–25 g (100–250 mL)
  • Glucagon only if no IV access
  • Transport after the first D10W dose or glucagon
slides.say: Here's how your job changes. In BC, decreased LOC with no known cause is covered by the Diabetic Emergencies protocol, so you'll use it often. The left column is your EMR routine: manage the airway, give oxygen to ninety-four percent, use the lateral or three-quarter prone position if needed, take vital signs with a sugar, and look for stroke signs. If the sugar is under four point oh and the patient can protect the airway, give glucose gel; if not, the EMR gives glucagon. The right column is new. The PCP starts an IV and corrects a confirmed low with D10W, ten to twenty-five grams. Glucagon becomes your backup when you can't get IV access.
slides.sayZh: 这里能看出你的工作怎么变了。在 BC，原因不明的意识下降归在糖尿病急症流程里，所以你会经常用到它。左栏是你作为 EMR 的常规：处理气道，给氧到九十四，必要时侧卧或四分之三俯卧位，测生命体征和血糖，并查卒中征象。血糖低于四点零、病人能保护气道，就给葡萄糖凝胶；不能的话，EMR 给胰高血糖素。右栏是新的：PCP 开静脉通路，用 D10W 十到二十五克纠正确认的低血糖。开不了静脉时，胰高血糖素才是你的备选。

slides.q: You're a PCP. A known diabetic is unresponsive; you've opened the airway. BGL is 2.1 mmol/L. What is your best next step?
options: Put glucose gel inside the cheek
Start an IV and give D10W, 10–25 g
Load and go; treat the sugar at the hospital
slides.say: Now a PCP decision. You're a PCP. A known diabetic is unresponsive, and you've opened the airway. The blood sugar is two point one. What is your best next step? A, put glucose gel inside the cheek. B, start an IV and give D10W, ten to twenty-five grams. C, give D50W, twenty-five grams IV push. D, load and go, and treat the sugar at the hospital. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 来一道 PCP 决策题。你是 PCP，一位已知糖尿病人没有反应，你已经开放了气道，血糖二点一。下一步最好怎么做？A 把葡萄糖凝胶放进颊内；B 开静脉，给 D10W 十到二十五克；C 静推 D50W 二十五克；D 立即转运，到医院再处理血糖。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. A confirmed low in a patient who can't protect the airway calls for IV dextrose, and in BC that's D10W, ten to twenty-five grams. If you can't get an IV, glucagon is your backup. A is wrong because oral glucose is only for a patient who can protect the airway. C is the book's drug, but BC has no D50W. D is wrong because BC has you transport after the first dose of D10W or glucagon, not before.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。病人不能保护气道、低血糖已确认，就要静脉补糖，在 BC 就是 D10W 十到二十五克。开不了静脉时，胰高血糖素是备选。A 错，口服葡萄糖只给能保护气道的病人。C 是书里的药，但 BC 没有 D50W。D 错，BC 流程要求给完第一剂 D10W 或胰高血糖素之后再转运，而不是之前。

slides.title: Naloxone: what changes for the PCP
slides.body:
• Ventilate first: BVM, two people if possible; SpO₂ ≥ 94%
  • Check the sugar; correct a low
  • BC: 0.4 → 0.4 → 0.8 → 2.0 mg IM/IV, reassess every 3 min
  • Or 4 mg intranasal
  • PCP adds: still unconscious and apneic → IV naloxone

Waking can be sudden: withdrawal, fear, aggression. Have help ready.
slides.say: Naloxone isn't new for you; EMRs give it too. What changes is the route. The BC overdose protocol starts with the airway: ventilate with a bag-valve mask, two people if you can, keep the saturation at ninety-four percent or more, and check the sugar. The BC dose ladder is zero point four, zero point four, zero point eight, then two milligrams, IM or IV, reassessing every three minutes, or four milligrams intranasal. Keep going until the saturation is at least ninety-four and breathing is over ten a minute. The PCP addition: if the patient stays unconscious and apneic, consider an IV and give naloxone intravenously. Patients can wake suddenly, afraid or aggressive, so have help ready.
slides.sayZh: 纳洛酮对你不是新药，EMR 也能给。变化在给药途径。BC 阿片过量流程先管气道：用球囊面罩通气，能两人操作就两人，血氧维持在九十四以上，并测血糖。BC 的剂量阶梯是零点四、零点四、零点八、再两毫克，肌注或静注，每三分钟评估一次；或者四毫克经鼻。直到血氧至少九十四、呼吸每分钟超过十次。PCP 多出的是：病人仍昏迷且呼吸暂停时，考虑开静脉、静脉给纳洛酮。病人可能突然醒来，恐惧或有攻击性，所以要备好人手。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• D10W leaking out of the vein can kill tissue: check the IV first
  • D10W for a confirmed low; recheck the sugar after
  • Slow pulse from high ICP: don't treat the pulse; notify and move
  • No routine hyperventilation; suction gently
  • Don't overload: no extra IV fluid without a reason
  • Entonox, methoxyflurane: not with decreased LOC
slides.say: Now the new risks that come with your new tools. First, D10W must go into a working vein; if it leaks into the tissue, it can cause tissue death, so check that the IV runs well before you give it. Second, give it for a confirmed low, and recheck the sugar after; the book warns that high sugar can make a stroke worse. Third, if a high-ICP patient has a slow pulse, the pressure is the cause. Don't chase the pulse; notify the hospital and transport. Fourth, no routine hyperventilation, and suction gently, because coughing and gagging raise ICP. Fifth, watch your IV volume. And BC's inhaled pain drugs, Entonox and methoxyflurane, are contraindicated with a decreased LOC.
slides.sayZh: 现在讲新工具带来的新风险。第一，D10W 必须进到通畅的静脉里，漏到组织里会造成组织坏死，所以给药前先确认静脉通畅。第二，D10W 只给确认的低血糖，给完要复测血糖；书里提醒高血糖会加重卒中。第三，颅内压高的病人脉搏慢，是压力造成的，不要去处理脉搏，要通知医院并转运。第四，不要常规过度通气，吸引要轻柔，因为呛咳和作呕会升高颅内压。第五，注意输液量。另外，BC 的两种吸入镇痛药，笑气和甲氧氟烷，意识下降时都禁用。

slides.title: For the BC exam
slides.body:
• Book: D50W 25 g → BC: D10W 10–25 g IV, PCP only
  • BC treats BGL < 4.0 mmol/L at every age
  • Book: naloxone 0.4–2 mg IV → BC: 0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 2.0 mg or 4 mg IN
  • Book: SpO₂ > 90% → BC protocols: ≥ 94%
  • Thiamine, benzodiazepines, atropine: not on the BC exam
  • EMRs have no IV; glucagon is the EMR's option
slides.say: Let's line up the book with BC. The book gives D50W, twenty-five grams. BC has no D50W; the PCP gives D10W, ten to twenty-five grams IV. BC treats a blood sugar under four point oh at every age. The book gives naloxone, zero point four to two milligrams IV; BC uses the ladder, zero point four, zero point four, zero point eight, two, IM or IV, or four milligrams intranasal. The book accepts a saturation over ninety percent; BC protocols aim for ninety-four or higher. Thiamine, benzodiazepines and atropine all appear in this chapter, but none are on the BC licensing exam. And EMRs have no IV, so glucagon is the EMR's option.
slides.sayZh: 把书和 BC 对一下。书里给 D50W 二十五克；BC 没有 D50W，PCP 给 D10W 十到二十五克静脉注射。BC 各年龄一律按血糖低于四点零处理。书里纳洛酮是零点四到两毫克静推；BC 用阶梯：零点四、零点四、零点八、两毫克，肌注或静注，或者四毫克经鼻。书里血氧高于百分之九十就可以；BC 流程要求九十四以上。本章出现的硫胺素、苯二氮卓类和阿托品，执照考试都不考。还有，EMR 没有静脉权限，所以胰高血糖素是 EMR 的选择。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. The brain needs oxygen, glucose, normal temperature; CPP = MAP − ICP
  2. Rising ICP: high BP, wide pulse pressure, slow pulse and breathing
  3. PCP adds an IV, D10W 10–25 g for a confirmed low, and IV naloxone

Next: stroke, TIA, seizures and syncope
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: the brain needs oxygen, glucose and a normal temperature, and its perfusion pressure is the MAP minus the ICP, so a high ICP or a low blood pressure can both starve it. Two: rising ICP looks like the opposite of shock: a high blood pressure, a wide pulse pressure, and a slow pulse and breathing. Three: for decreased LOC, the PCP adds an IV, D10W ten to twenty-five grams for a confirmed low, and IV naloxone when the patient stays unconscious and apneic. Next lesson, we'll look at stroke, TIA, seizures and syncope. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，大脑需要氧、葡萄糖和正常体温，脑灌注压等于 MAP 减 ICP，所以颅内压高或血压低都会让大脑缺血。二，颅内压升高的表现和休克正好相反：血压高、脉压宽、脉搏和呼吸慢。三，意识下降时，PCP 多了静脉通路、确认低血糖时给 D10W 十到二十五克，以及病人持续昏迷且呼吸暂停时的静脉纳洛酮。下节课讲卒中、TIA、癫痫发作和晕厥。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
